instruments.name: Problematic AI use index (Problematic Use Scale; three-item symptom index based on ICD-11 behavioral addiction criteria)
instruments.source_citation: Author-developed for this study (Ignatowski, Duczmal, & Moskalewicz, 2026); based on ICD-11 criteria for behavioral addictions; no separate development paper cited
instruments.response_scale: 5-point agreement scale (1 = strongly disagree, 5 = strongly agree)
instruments.subscales: None; summed (reported as mean) index of symptom severity. The items cover priority given to AI use / disruption of life balance, loss of control (more use than intended), and continued use despite negative consequences. Not treated as a homogeneous latent scale.
instruments.adapted_from: Not adapted from an existing scale; based on ICD-11 behavioral addiction criteria
items: Using AI chatbots noticeably changes the balance between different areas of my life (e.g., study, relationships, rest).
I sometimes use an AI chatbot more often than I originally intended.
I sometimes continue using an AI chatbot even though I know it is not good for me (e.g., it takes time, distracts me, lowers my mood).

codes.note: Items appear as English translations; the Polish originals are not printed. The report says the index is not a diagnostic tool. α = .685 in this sample of N = 102 teachers.

instruments.name: Generative AI Dependency Scale
instruments.source_citation: Goh, A. Y. H., Hartanto, A., & Majeed, N. M. (2025). Generative Artificial Intelligence Dependency: Scale Development, Validation, and its Motivational, Behavioral, and Psychological Correlates. Computers in Human Behavior Reports, 100845. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.chbr.2025.100845 (this report)
instruments.response_scale: 5-point Likert, 1 = Strongly disagree to 5 = Strongly agree
instruments.subscales: Cognitive Preoccupation (Salience and Compulsive Use) (3 items); Negative Consequences (4 items); Withdrawal (4 items). Subscale score = mean of its items; total = mean of the three subscale scores; higher-order dependency factor
instruments.adapted_from: Items adapted from smartphone and social media dependency measures (Chen, 2015; Liu & Ma, 2018; Ünal & Deniz, 2015); based on Goodman's (1990) behavioral dependency framework
items: My decisions are often influenced by generative AI.
I feel an urge to use generative AI, even when it may not be necessary.
I look forward to using generative AI, even if it is unrelated to the task at hand.
My use of generative AI has caused concerns for me.
I have trouble completing work or other responsibilities without generative AI.
I feel less confident in my abilities without generative AI.
My use of generative AI has negatively affected my problem-solving skills or efficiency.
I experience restlessness if I am unable to use generative AI.
I feel unsettled or distracted when I cannot use generative AI.
I feel a sense of disconnection when I cannot access generative AI.
I get frustrated or irritable when I am unable to use generative AI.

instruments.name: Generative AI Addiction scale
instruments.source_citation: Zhou, T., & Zhang, C. (2024). Examining generative AI user addiction from a C-A-C perspective. Technology in Society, 78, Article 102653. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.techsoc.2024.102653
instruments.response_scale: 7-point Likert, 1 = Strongly disagree to 7 = Strongly agree
items: Using generative AI sometimes interferes with my other activities (such as study and work).
I feel a bit uneasy when I cannot use generative AI.
I find it difficult to control my using generative AI.

codes.note: The GAIDS is the main instrument. It began as 30 items (7-point), then 30 items (5-point), then 20; only the final 11 are printed, the earlier sets are in ResearchBox #3834. Studies 3 and 5 gave 20 items but analysed 11. The Zhou & Zhang scale was used only for convergent validity (Study 5).
